bugs: Authorization runs after FormRequest validation (Gate::authorize inside the controller at app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:41). A non-author sending an invalid payload (e.g. title='') gets 422 with validation errors instead of 403. Confirmed with a probe.
GET /api/posts?status= (empty) returns 422: ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns it into null, and 'sometimes' + Rule::enum without 'nullable' rejects it (impl-2 and impl-3 behave the same way).
antipatterns: routes/api.php:6 – adds the 'web' middleware group (session + CSRF) to API routes. This is unusual for a JSON API and will 419 non-SPA clients outside tests.
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:41,54 – Gate::authorize in the controller body instead of route-level ->can()/policy middleware, so validation runs before authorization.
app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:18 – 'tags.*' lacks 'required', so a null element only fails on the 'string' rule. Works, but the intent is unclear.
app/Models/Post.php:60 – trim() is redundant because the global TrimStrings middleware already trims.
app/Policies/PostPolicy.php:17 – delete delegates to update. Fine, but it couples the two abilities.
strengths: Idiomatic Laravel 12/13 model: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy] and #[Scope] attributes, a casts() method and an enum cast.
whereRelation for the tag filter, when() for conditional filters, latest()->latest('id') as a deterministic tie-break, withQueryString().
Observer handles slug uniqueness and published_at; `??=` respects a factory-provided slug.
Thorough tests (26): mass-assignment guard (slug/user_id/published_at ignored), unpublishing keeps published_at, combined filters, pagination, validation messages, 404.
Store returns 201 automatically through the resource's wasRecentlyCreated, with no ceremony.

bugs: GET /api/posts?status= (empty) returns 422 instead of being ignored (minor; shared by all three).
antipatterns: routes/api.php:7-11 – five hand-written routes (separate PUT and PATCH) where Route::apiResource('posts', ...)->except('show') plus ->can middleware would be shorter.

app/Http/Requests/StorePostRequest.php:25 – tagNames() helper exists only on StorePostRequest, while update uses $request->validated('tags') directly. This is an inconsistent, near-pointless abstraction.
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:20 – $request->enum('status') reads raw input rather than validated data (safe only because of the validation rule).
strengths: Authorization through route ->can('update','post') middleware, so a non-author gets 403 before validation. This is tested, including the invalid-payload case.
The thinnest controller: no authorization calls, $request->integer('per_page', 15), $request->enum(), and an eager-load column constraint ('tags:id,name').
Observer uses `$post->published_at ??= now()`, which is concise. The model uses Laravel 12+ attributes (#[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope]) and generic @use HasFactory annotations.
'tags.*' => required; 'sometimes','required' on update so a blank title is rejected.
Strongest test suite (26 tests, 94 assertions): default page size, last_page, both PUT and PATCH, non-author with invalid payload → 403, assertModelMissing.

bugs: 'distinct' on tags.* (StorePostRequest.php:21, UpdatePostRequest.php:21) rejects a tag array with duplicates (including ' php ' vs 'php' after trimming) with 422 instead of de-duplicating. This is a stricter, less forgiving reading of 'tags created on the fly from an array of names'.
antipatterns: app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:23 – adds global Model::shouldBeStrict(), which is unrelated to the task and changes app-wide behaviour.
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:48 – ->response()->setStatusCode(201) is unnecessary ceremony; JsonResource already returns 201 for wasRecentlyCreated models.
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:22-28 – HasMiddleware with string 'can:update,post' middleware in the controller. Route-level ->can() on the resource is more direct.
app/Models/Post.php:50 – trim() is redundant with the TrimStrings middleware, and unique() runs after N firstOrCreate queries rather than before.
Docblock noise (@return array<string, mixed> on every rules()/definition()).
strengths: Authorization via controller middleware runs before validation, so a non-author gets 403. This is tested.
apiResource()->except('show') with a single auth group keeps routes clean.
Same modern model idioms: attributes, enum cast, #[Scope], whereRelation, a deterministic latest()->latest('id').
Tests cover guests, slug collisions, preserved published_at, tag retention/clearing, combined filters and pagination, and use the factory magic hasTags().

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-2 first, impl-3 second and impl-1 third. impl-2 and impl-3 are close; the main split is a real authorization-ordering bug in impl-1.

**How I checked**
- All three test suites pass: impl-1 26 tests, impl-2 26 tests, impl-3 19 tests.
- I ran throwaway probe tests against each implementation and deleted them afterwards. They covered: a non-author sending an invalid payload, tags with whitespace, case differences, empty or null elements and duplicates, an empty status filter, a non-numeric per_page, ordering when timestamps are identical, punctuation-only titles, and an unauthenticated request that doesn't ask for JSON.

**What all three share**
- Nearly the same architecture: enum, #[Fillable]/#[ObservedBy]/#[Scope] attributes, an observer that generates the slug and sets published_at, whereRelation for the tag filter, latest()->latest('id'), withQueryString(), and the same resource.
- All three return 422 for `?status=` (empty) rather than ignoring it.
- Laravel's default auth redirect makes all three return 500 for an unauthenticated request that doesn't ask for JSON, because no login route exists.

**impl-2 (rank 1)**
- Authorizes with route-level ->can(), so a non-author gets 403 before validation, as the task asks.
- Has the thinnest controller ($request->integer, $request->enum, eager-loading only tags:id,name).
- Has the most complete tests, including default page size and a non-author with an invalid payload.
- Weak points: verbose hand-written PUT/PATCH routes and a one-off tagNames() helper.

**impl-3 (rank 2)**
- Also authorizes before validation, through controller middleware.
- Adds a global Model::shouldBeStrict() unrelated to the task.
- Sets the 201 status by hand, which isn't needed.
- Rejects duplicate tag names with 'distinct' instead of de-duplicating them.
- Has a thinner test suite (19 tests; it doesn't test that a client-supplied slug or owner is ignored, or the default page size).

**impl-1 (rank 3)**
- Has strong tests and clean code.
- It calls Gate::authorize inside the controller, after the form request has validated, so a non-author's invalid PUT returns 422 instead of the required 403. I confirmed this with a probe.
- It puts the 'web' middleware group (session and CSRF) on the API routes.
- I weighted this real deviation from the 403 rule above impl-3's design choices.
